test_1_socket_reconnect_catchup.name: App-side wiring (7.3.A SessionView socketStatus + 7.3.B sync onReconnected lastVisibleSessionId)
test_1_socket_reconnect_catchup.method: Used Playwright BrowserContext.setOffline(true) for ~2.5s, then setOffline(false), monitored network requests. Cycled twice for reproducibility.
test_1_socket_reconnect_catchup.expected: On websocket reconnect (after Internet restored), the app should fire incremental REST GET /v3/sessions/<visible>/messages?after_seq=N (catch-up) and re-invalidate sync caches (sessions, machines, feed, etc).
test_1_socket_reconnect_catchup.observed: Both reconnect cycles produced exactly this pattern. After offline transition, requests failed with ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED. After online transition: (a) fresh GETs to /v1/sessions, /v1/machines, /v1/artifacts, /v1/friends, /v1/feed, /v1/account/profile (cache invalidations from sync.ts onReconnected callback); (b) GET /v3/sessions/cmoedofgz86n5nz15xsldnk35/messages?after_seq=22&limit=100 fires within ~1s of reconnect for the currently visible session — this is the exact behavior 7.3.A and 7.3.B were meant to enable.
test_1_socket_reconnect_catchup.evidence: Network requests captured via mcp__playwright__browser_network_requests. Two complete offline→online cycles each produced visible-session catch-up fetch.

test_2_hydrate_preserve.name: Hydrate preserve-if-recent (7.3.C)
test_2_hydrate_preserve.method: Source-level verification: sync.ts:818-828 contains the conditional preserveThinking branch. Runtime path is: fetchSessions decrypt loop reads existingSession from storage.getState().sessions[id], checks existingSession.thinking===true AND Date.now()-session.activeAt<5000ms.
test_2_hydrate_preserve.expected: If a session was thinking=true locally AND activeAt is within 5s, app preserves thinking on hydrate; otherwise resets to false.
test_2_hydrate_preserve.observed: Source present and structurally correct (see deployed_components_verified). However, the preserve branch can only fire when existingSession.thinking===true at hydrate time. Because pipeline 7.1 is not deployed and the CLI is silent on bg-task thinking emits, no actively-thinking session in this test had local thinking=true. Therefore the preserve branch never executed during this verification window. The negative branch (reset to false) executed correctly with no regression observed.
test_2_hydrate_preserve.evidence: Source code confirms logic; absence of CLI-side thinking emits prevented exercising the preserve branch in this run.
test_2_hydrate_preserve.caveat: This sub-fix's full value is contingent on 7.1 producing a thinking=true emission in the first place. As the BA spec correctly noted: 'If 7.2 ships: snapshot arrives within ~1s; preserve window bridges. If 7.2 misses: 5s preserve gives CLI's next 2s session-alive ephemeral time to arrive (CLI heartbeat is volatile.emit every 2s). If session truly idle: activeAt older than 5s, preserve=false.' All three paths require something to emit thinking=true upstream — which 7.1 was supposed to ensure but was not deployed.

test_3_server_snapshot.name: Server snapshot on connect (7.2)
test_3_server_snapshot.method: Source verification of socket.ts:115-183 (sendSessionSnapshotsToConnectingSocket → broadcastConnectActivity → handleConnection chain) plus runtime probe via /v2/sessions/active to confirm DB-side session state is fresh; observed offline/online cycles to look for ephemeral activity events on connect.
test_3_server_snapshot.expected: On user-scoped websocket connect, server queries thinkingCache.getActivitySnapshotForUser(userId), then for each recently-active session emits an ephemeral 'activity' event with thinking flag (true if cache has fresh entry, else false) directly to the connecting socket.
test_3_server_snapshot.observed: Source structurally correct. Live behavior depends on thinkingCache being populated by recordThinking() calls from sessionUpdateHandler.handleSessionAlive(). For thinkingCache to contain thinking=true, the CLI must have emitted session-alive with thinking=true within the last 5s. Pipeline 7.1 (CLI keepAlive scope/fresh-emit fix) is the producer of those emits — without it, every cache lookup returns thinking=false, and every emitted snapshot frame carries thinking=false. The server code path executes; the data it carries is structurally insufficient by itself. WebSocket frame inspection via injected hook returned 0 frames because the underlying transport is engine.io polling-then-upgrade and the upgrade window did not capture frames in the inspection wrapper; fallback evidence is the /v2/sessions/active probe (confirming active=true sessions have fresh activeAt within 10s, which means session-alive heartbeats ARE flowing — but they carry thinking=false from old CLI).
test_3_server_snapshot.evidence: Source code present and wired; runtime activeAt freshness confirms server-side path is alive. WebSocket-frame-level capture inconclusive due to transport upgrade timing — not a regression, just a measurement limitation.
test_3_server_snapshot.limitation: Could not directly observe an emitted ephemeral activity frame with thinking=true in the WebSocket because (a) the active session being tested is itself this conversation, which is in a tool-output state (not in a 'claude is producing text' state), so even a working CLI would emit thinking=false here; and (b) there is no other dev-account session currently in mid-turn output state to test against.

all_findings.issue: Pipeline 7.1 (CLI keepAlive session-scope + fresh emit on bg-task wake) is NOT deployed. The dev daemon is still running pre-fix dist/index.mjs from before this cycle, so the CLI never emits a fresh thinking=true ephemeral on bg-task wake. all_findings.recommendation: User must (a) authorise daemon restart via /root/bin/safe-daemon-restart.sh dev or accept PAUSE-PENDING-USER for 7.1, OR (b) accept that current cycle resolves AC for message catch-up only and explicitly defers indicator real-time refresh to a follow-up.

all_findings.issue: Could not directly observe ephemeral activity frame with thinking=true in browser DevTools because (a) Socket.io uses polling-then-upgrade transport which the test rig's WebSocket constructor hook didn't intercept after upgrade; (b) no actively-mid-turn session existed in the dev account during the verification window.
all_findings.recommendation: Future QA cycles for ephemeral verification should either: (1) inject test instrumentation in the app to log received ephemeral events, or (2) coordinate a session that is reliably mid-turn during the verification window.
